speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition better, could you tell me when the rash first appeared and whether it is raised or flat? Also, have you started any new medications or eaten any unusual foods recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: The progression of symptoms, particularly the facial rash sparing the perioral area following a week of viral-like symptoms, is highly suggestive of Fifth Disease (Erythema Infectiosum). To confirm this, has the rash on her cheeks had a "slapped cheek" appearance, and has it since spread to her arms and legs in a lacy, reticular pattern?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of a "slapped cheek" facial rash sparing the perioral area followed by a lacy, pruritic body rash after a mild viral prodrome is classic for Parvovirus B19 infection. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
